ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher under NS-7; no account flag on the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeX is a non-metered service and the only disputed item is the $6.61 cancellation fee [F4][F7], so the fee stands only through NS-0's driver-cancellation branch, which routes a driver no-show claim to NS-1 [RD-? ] — concretely, NS-0 requires all of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) [F4][NS-0].

The first two elements are met and are not in dispute. NS-1(i): the trace and record show a driver tap ("I'm Here") at 14:14:10, not a platform auto-confirmation, and the platform separately logged arrival at 14:13:25 [F5][F6][NS-1]. NS-1(ii): at the tap the GPS placed the driver 41 m from the pickup, and the closest approach across the episode was 38 m, inside the 200 m radius [F1][F6][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) fails on the system records, which override the driver's later statements. After the 14:14:10 tap the driver stayed within 200 m for only 1 min 40 s (100 s), against the threshold of more than 3 minutes (180 s), until cancellation at 14:15:50 [F6][F4][NS-1]. The most generous alternative readings are still short: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 25 s, the platform arrival-to-cancellation gap was the same 2 min 25 s, and the stationary period at 41 m was 2 min 0 s [F2][F3][F5][NS-1]. The driver's in-app claim "3 min up, cancelling the trip" [F10] and his post-trip statement that he waited and cancelled as a no-show [F12] are contradicted by the timeline and cannot cure the shortfall [F4][F6][NS-1].

Because a driver-cancellation no-show charge requires all of NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) and (iii) is unmet, the $6.61 has no charging ground and must be refunded in full (as a Ryde voucher, NS-7): the fee charged was $6.61 with 1.0× surge, so the refundable amount is $6.61, not a computed detour figure [F7][F8][NS-0][NS-2][NS-7].

The rider's request for an account-review flag is rejected. RD-6 attaches only where this case itself is upheld against the driver via a route-deviation finding (RD-2 refund or recorded RD-1 breach); here the trip was cancelled with no off-route segment, and NS-2's only flag condition — a fake "I'm Here" confirmation while not at the pickup — is not met, as the driver was 41 m from the pickup at the tap [F1][F6][F13][F14][F15][RD-2][RD-6][NS-2]. Profile facts are therefore not used to decide either way [F16][F17][RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: RD-6 requires this case itself to be upheld against the driver through a route-deviation finding (RD-2 refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach). The trip was cancelled by the driver with no off-route segment, so no RD-2 refund arises and no breach is recorded [F4][F13][F14][F15][RD-6][RD-2]. The driver's 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days [F17] cannot support the flag, because RD-6 is a route-deviation clause and profile facts cannot decide the case [F17][RD-6].

Accepted as far as it states the rider's record is clean [F16], but a clean profile is not an element of NS-2 and cannot decide the fee either way; the refund rests on the failed NS-1(iii) wait, not on the rider's history [F16][F6][NS-2].
Correct that NS-1(i) is met by the driver tap at 14:14:10 [F6], but meeting (i) alone does not make the fee chargeable, since NS-1 requires (i)(ii)(iii) together [F6][NS-1].
Correct that NS-1(ii) is met (41 m at the tap, closest 38 m) [F1][F6], but this element alone does not establish the charge; the case turns on (iii), which fails [F6][NS-1].

The driver's profile (924 days, 4.53 rating, 815 trips in 90 d) [F17] cannot decide the no-show finding under NS-1/NS-2; the system records of the wait control, and they show the threshold unmet [F6][F2][F5][NS-1][NS-2].
Correctly conceded against the driver: the post-trip statement [F12] cannot cure the sub-three-minute wait measured by GPS and timeline [F6][F3].
